newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU parliament, Commissioner attack Chirac on China.
newsitem.headline: EU parliament, Commissioner attack Chirac on China.

text.p: The European Parliament on Thursday delivered its third snub to French President Jaques Chirac, slamming Paris for blocking formal United Nations condemnation of China's human rights record.

The attack, which was backed up by EU commissioner Hans van den Broek, came as Chirac, who is in the throes of an election campaign, arrived in Beijing for a four-day visit expected to lead to the signing of business deals worth hundreds of millions of dollars and set the seal on strong political ties.

"The European Parliament (regrets) that the EU failed to speak with one voice and present a common resolution on the human rights situation in China," the EU assembly said in a resolution which won cross-party support.
"This lack of unity takes the wind out of our sails when it comes to human rights," van den Broek told the assembly during a debate on China in which Chirac was personally criticised several times.

This latest snub follows European Parliament criticism in March of a controversial new French law clamping down on immigration and protests in 1995 and 1996 about Chirac's decision to resume French nuclear tests in the Pacific.

China came under fire from the UN Human Rights Commission meeting in Geneva in March and April but escaped formal censure after France refused to back a critical motion tabled by Denmark, with support from Ireland and the Netherlands.
Germany, Greece, Italy and Spain later withdrew their support for the European motion.

In every other year since the 1989 crackdown on pro-democracy protesters in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, the 15-member European Union has unanimously called for the UN to condemn China for human rights violations.
The parliament's resolution went on to attack China for subsequently halting Danish and Dutch trade missions and threatening further retaliatory measures.

In another swipe at both Beijing and Paris, van den Broek said "China has to be told it is not on to discriminate between member states of the Union when it comes to human rights policy. I do hope that President Chirac will use his visit to China to forward that message."

Parliament's resolution quoted China's Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang as saying "China...will delay important changes of officials...and halt exchanges and cooperation with Denmark on human rights...Denmark has set up obstacles to the smooth development of relations between the two countries."
Chirac received a red carpet welcome at Beijing's Capital Airport where he was greeted by Wang Zhongyu, chairman of the State Economic and Trade Commission.

The French president was accompanied by some 60 heads of major French enterprises. He will meet his Chinese counterpart Jiang Zemin in Beijing and oversee the signing of lucrative business deals for French industry.
He was also due to visit Shanghai, China's booming commercial hub, to open an exhibition on French technology, before leaving on Sunday.
